explanation: n! / (n-k)! telescopes: every factor of (n-k)! cancels, leaving just the k factors n, n-1, ..., n-k+1. A loop that runs k times multiplying an accumulator (started at 1, the empty product) by n - i computes exactly that, so k = 0 falls out naturally with no special case. Declaring the accumulator long matters -- 20! is about 2.4 quintillion, far beyond int range but within long's.
hints: You never need factorials: nPk(5, 2) is just 5 * 4 -- k factors counting down from n.
Initialize long result = 1L and loop i from 0 to k-1, multiplying result by (n - i).
Starting at 1 makes k == 0 return 1 automatically -- the empty product needs no if statement.
